PLAY TIME

HOOK

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Unfinished material needs a boundary, not denial.

GAME MOVE
Begin Imagine Container; hinge on Name Stored. Last decision: Close Container.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Imagine Container — Imagine a container whose lock, size, material, and location feel credible.
2. Place Cannot — Place only what cannot be processed now inside it.
3. Name Stored — Name what is stored and when it will be revisited, ideally with support.
4. Close Container — Close the container and reorient to today’s next task.

FINISH MOVE — Let Close Container be enough.

Close Container is enough for The Secure Pending Box if unfinished material needs a boundary, not denial.

rituals.title: BUILD SAFE-ENOUGH, NOT PERFECT
rituals.name: BUILD SAFE-ENOUGH, NOT PERFECT
rituals.hook: Build Safe-Enough, Not Perfect gives Trauma time collapse a boundary. Only this matters: A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.
rituals.recognition_cue: Build Safe-Enough, Not Perfect gives Trauma time collapse a boundary. Only this matters: A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.
rituals.goal: A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.
rituals.mission: A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.
rituals.challenge: A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.
rituals.immediate_need: A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.
rituals.game_move: Begin Place Five; hinge on Rehearse Specific. Nothing follows Strengthen here.
rituals.unique_game_move: Begin Place Five; hinge on Rehearse Specific. Nothing follows Strengthen here.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Trauma & memory-as-present

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Build Safe-Enough, Not Perfect gives Trauma time collapse a boundary. Only this matters: A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.

GAME MOVE
Begin Place Five; hinge on Rehearse Specific. Nothing follows Strengthen here.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Place Five — Construct a place using five sensory facts and one control feature: an exit, boundary, companion, or adjustable distance.
2. Rehearse Specific — Rehearse entering through a specific cue and leaving on purpose.
3. Strengthen — Strengthen the detail that produces the clearest bodily yes.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
The practical win in Build Safe-Enough, Not Perfect: a believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure. End at Strengthen.
rituals.formula_flow: Place Five → Rehearse Specific → Strengthen
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Abandon imagery that attracts threat memories or increases unreality.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: ONE-WORD LIGHT TOUCH
rituals.name: ONE-WORD LIGHT TOUCH
rituals.hook: One-Word Light Touch tests Scarcity thinking directly. Only this matters: Name enough to see; not enough to build a story.
rituals.recognition_cue: One-Word Light Touch tests Scarcity thinking directly. Only this matters: Name enough to see; not enough to build a story.
rituals.goal: Name enough to see; not enough to build a story.
rituals.mission: Name enough to see; not enough to build a story.
rituals.challenge: Name enough to see; not enough to build a story.
rituals.immediate_need: Name enough to see; not enough to build a story.
rituals.game_move: Use Apply Quiet; work through Use Word. Nothing follows Name Producing here.
rituals.unique_game_move: Use Apply Quiet; work through Use Word. Nothing follows Name Producing here.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Values, meaning & loss

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
One-Word Light Touch tests Scarcity thinking directly. Only this matters: Name enough to see; not enough to build a story.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Name enough to see; not enough to build a story.

GAME MOVE
Use Apply Quiet; work through Use Word. Nothing follows Name Producing here.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Apply Quiet — As events arise, apply a quiet category: hearing, planning, heat, remembering, pressure.
2. Use Word — Use one word once, then return to the raw event.
3. Name Producing — If a Name starts producing analysis, Name that ‘explaining’ and release it.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
One-Word Light Touch gives one sign: name enough to see; not enough to build a story. Finish there, not beyond Name Producing.
rituals.formula_flow: Apply Quiet → Use Word → Name Producing

rituals.hook: Bring Close The Micro-Gaps to Attention fragmentation. Let this change: Meditative flow is repaired one break at a time.
rituals.recognition_cue: Bring Close The Micro-Gaps to Attention fragmentation. Let this change: Meditative flow is repaired one break at a time.
rituals.goal: Meditative flow is repaired one break at a time.

rituals.immediate_need: Meditative flow is repaired one break at a time.
rituals.game_move: 4 moves: Choose Precise into Track Interval. Let Practice arrives; experiment over.
rituals.unique_game_move: 4 moves: Choose Precise into Track Interval. Let Practice arrives; experiment over.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Attention & cognitive overload

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
Bring Close The Micro-Gaps to Attention fragmentation. Let this change: Meditative flow is repaired one break at a time.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Meditative flow is repaired one break at a time.

GAME MOVE
4 moves: Choose Precise into Track Interval. Let Practice arrives; experiment over.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Precise — Choose an anchor and notice the precise moment contact breaks.
2. Return Instead — Instead of judging the distraction, shorten the delay before returning.
3. Track Interval — Track the interval between noticing and reconnection.
4. Let Practice — Let practice end after one stretch with visibly fewer or shorter gaps.

FINISH MOVE — Complete Let Practice, then return to your day.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Call Close The Micro-Gaps complete here: meditative flow is repaired one break at a time. Stop the game at Let Practice.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Precise → Return Instead → Track Interval → Let Practice
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Release focus if effort becomes rigid, painful, or compulsive.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.game_move: Take Pick Word; keep Flash Image literal. After Jump Letter, return.
rituals.unique_game_move: Take Pick Word; keep Flash Image literal. After Jump Letter, return.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Rigid beliefs, labels & stories

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

HOOK
Break The Night'S Storyline loosens Narrative overbuilding. Purpose: Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.

GAME MOVE
Take Pick Word; keep Flash Image literal. After Jump Letter, return.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Pick Word — Choose one harmless five-letter word, such as TABLE. Use each letter once; there is no need to finish perfectly.
2. Call Object — For the first letter, name a neutral object beginning with it—T for tree, for example.
3. Flash Image — Picture that object for about two seconds with no action, meaning, memory, or story.
4. Jump Letter — Jump to the next letter and a completely unrelated object. End after five letters; do not score sleep.

FINISH MOVE — Jump Letter is your cue to stop.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Break The Night'S Storyline earns its finish: sleep does not need another storyline to solve. Once Jump Letter happens, stop.
rituals.formula_flow: Pick Word → Call Object → Flash Image → Jump Letter
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use only while safely resting; never while driving. Stop if images become distressing, compulsive, or disorienting.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

TRIGGER
Perfectionism & performance pressure

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
Make The First Move Deliberately Wrong loosens Perfectionism. Keep the task narrow: A throwaway mistake can make the first move lose its authority.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A throwaway mistake can make the first move lose its authority.

GAME MOVE
Take Throwaway; keep Fix One literal. Stopping line: Continue Clean.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Throwaway — Open a private mental sandbox and mark it THROWAWAY—NOT FOR SENDING.
2. Make Wrong — Imagine one obviously imperfect start: a clumsy first sentence, rough title, messy mental sketch, or unfinished opening.
3. Fix One — Correct exactly one useful part without polishing the rest.
4. Continue Clean — Keep working only if the task now feels editable; otherwise keep the corrected fragment in mind and stop cleanly.

FINISH MOVE — Continue Clean is your cue to stop.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Make The First Move Deliberately Wrong earns its finish: a throwaway mistake can make the blank page lose its authority. Final marker: Continue Clean.
rituals.formula_flow: Throwaway → Make Wrong → Fix One → Continue Clean

PAUSE
Never use deliberate errors in medical, legal, financial, safety-critical, submitted, or live shared work.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

TRIGGER
Values, meaning & loss

1–2 minutes

HOOK
Self-Respect Checksum challenges Value disconnection briefly. Test this: A conversation should not corrupt your own values.

GOAL
A conversation should not corrupt your own values.

GAME MOVE
Start at Respond Verify; next, Revise Sentence. Close with Speak Extra.

2. Revise Sentence — Revise any sentence that fails the checksum.
3. Speak Extra — Then speak without extra justification.

1. See The Person — Imagine the person in front of you.

rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Rigid beliefs, labels & stories

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

HOOK
The Twenty-Minute Truth Story challenges Narrative overbuilding briefly. Keep the lens here: A private story can help your mind make sense of an event.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A private story can help your mind make sense of an event.

GAME MOVE
Start at Set A Time; next, Come Back To Now. Finish Repeat Only If Helpful; skip rechecking.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Set A Time — Choose up to twenty minutes.
2. Tell The Story — In your mind, move through what happened, what you felt, and what it means now.

rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Picture — Picture having lost access to your current life and unexpectedly waking inside it again.
2. Small — What small feature would suddenly matter—someone’s voice, a body ability, unfinished work, morning light?
3. Choose Behaviour — Choose one behaviour that honours that recovered value today, without romanticising real hardship.

FINISH MOVE — Complete Choose Behaviour, then return to your day.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Language can lower heat without lowering truth.

GAME MOVE
Run Underline; let Observe Behaviour work. Final beat: Read Action.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Underline — Underline absolutes and inflammatory terms in your account.
2. Observe Behaviour — Exchange every one for a precise factual equivalent: ‘always’ becomes the actual frequency; ‘destroyed’ becomes the specific loss; ‘evil’ becomes the observed behaviour.
3. Read Action — Re-read and notice what action the cooler version supports.

FINISH MOVE — Read Action is your cue to stop.

HOOK

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Absence becomes evidence only after prediction says what should be present.

GAME MOVE
Keep Ask Sign small; move through Mark Absence. Name Explanation lands; leave it.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Ask Sign — Ask what sign must exist right now if the feared model is correct.
2. Search Fairly — Search once, fairly.
3. Mark Absence — If it is absent, Keep that absence and reduce—not erase—the model’s weight.
4. Name Explanation — Name the alternate explanation strengthened by the missing sign.

FINISH MOVE — Name Explanation closes the round.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Look For The Missing Danger is useful when: absence becomes evidence only after prediction says what should be present. Let Name Explanation be enough.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Emotion maintains itself through tempo as well as story.

GAME MOVE
Begin Cadence; no side task before Choose Opposite. Exit at Observe Emotional.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Cadence — Notice the cadence of speech, movement, or breathing.
2. Choose Opposite — Choose an opposite rhythm: agitated becomes deliberate, collapsed becomes lightly brisk, looping becomes irregular.
3. Observe Emotional — Maintain the new tempo through one simple task and observe the emotional shift.

FINISH MOVE — Observe Emotional closes the round.

WIN SIGNAL
The useful residue of Change The Rhythm, Change The State: emotion maintains itself through tempo as well as story. Stop with Observe Emotional.

rituals.title: THE MEMORY DOES NOT END THERE
rituals.name: THE MEMORY DOES NOT END THERE
rituals.ritual_name: THE MEMORY DOES NOT END THERE
rituals.hook: The painful scene was not the whole timeline. THE MEMORY DOES NOT END THERE follows the sequence far enough to include escape, endurance, help, or survival.
rituals.recognition_cue: The painful scene was not the whole timeline. THE MEMORY DOES NOT END THERE follows the sequence far enough to include escape, endurance, help, or survival.
rituals.goal: Pain may be stored without its later survival chapter.
rituals.mission: Pain may be stored without its later survival chapter.
rituals.challenge: Pain may be stored without its later survival chapter.
rituals.immediate_need: Pain may be stored without its later survival chapter.
rituals.game_move: End Retell to Don't Invent; no rewind. Endpoint: Restore.
rituals.unique_game_move: End Retell to Don't Invent; no rewind. Endpoint: Restore.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Automatic habits & autopilot

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

HOOK
The painful scene was not the whole timeline. THE MEMORY DOES NOT END THERE follows the sequence far enough to include escape, endurance, help, or survival.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Pain may be stored without its later survival chapter.

GAME MOVE
End Retell to Don't Invent; no rewind. Endpoint: Restore.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. End Retell — Retell only enough to reach the painful ending.
2. Follow Escape — Then append what actually followed: escape, help, adaptation, learning, regained ability, or today’s status.
3. Don't Invent — Do not invent redemption.
4. Restore — Restore the omitted chronology.

WIN SIGNAL

rituals.formula_flow: End Retell → Follow Escape → Don't Invent → Restore

rituals.title: ENTER THROUGH A RANDOM DOOR
rituals.name: ENTER THROUGH A RANDOM DOOR
rituals.hook: Starting can be harder than doing. ENTER THROUGH A RANDOM DOOR lets chance remove the argument over which safe beginning is best.
rituals.recognition_cue: Starting can be harder than doing. ENTER THROUGH A RANDOM DOOR lets chance remove the argument over which safe beginning is best.
rituals.goal: When the doorway is the problem, let chance choose a safe entrance.

rituals.challenge: When the doorway is the problem, let chance choose a safe entrance.

PLAY TIME

HOOK

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
When the doorway is the problem, let chance choose a safe entrance.

GAME MOVE
Number Doors to Enter There; no rewind. Leave it at Progress.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Number Doors — Name three to six task sections that can safely be done in any order and give each one a number.
2. Let Chance Choose — Use a random-number tool on your phone to choose one number. Do not pick again just because you dislike the number.
3. Enter There — Work only inside that section for ninety seconds; do not reorganise the whole project.
4. Mark Progress — Notice one concrete sign of progress, then decide whether to choose another number or stop.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Enter Through A Random Door did its job if: when the doorway is the problem, let chance choose a safe entrance. Do not grade Mark Progress.
rituals.formula_flow: Number Doors → Let Chance Choose → Enter There → Mark Progress
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use this only for reorderable work; never randomise required safety, medical, legal, financial, or technical sequences.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

PLAY TIME

HOOK
Borrow Stillness From The Wall gives Sensory disconnection less space. Aim: Let an unmoving object prove that movement is not the whole field.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Let an unmoving object prove that movement is not the whole field.

GAME MOVE
Use Rest Gaze; stay concrete through Don't Match. Stop at Let Facts.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Rest Gaze — Rest your gaze on a stable line, corner, or heavy object.
2. Compare Visual — Compare its visual constancy with the motion inside your body and mind.
3. Don't Match — Do not make the inner movement match.
4. Let Facts — Let both facts coexist until the outer reference becomes usable.

FINISH MOVE — Let Let Facts be enough.

rituals.game_move: Use Identify Nearest; stay concrete through Move Attention. Endpoint: Let Far.
rituals.unique_game_move: Use Identify Nearest; stay concrete through Move Attention. Endpoint: Let Far.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Urgency & decision pressure

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

HOOK
Sort The Sounds By Distance gives Urgency bias less space. Target: Urgency shrinks when hearing regains depth.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Urgency shrinks when hearing regains depth.

GAME MOVE
Use Identify Nearest; stay concrete through Move Attention. Endpoint: Let Far.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Identify Nearest — Spot the nearest sound, one mid-distance sound, and the farthest audible layer.
2. Move Attention — Move attention outward through those distances, then back once.
3. Let Far — Let the far sound widen the perceived space around the closest one.

Use Mask Names; stay concrete through Rank Blind. Last decision: Reveal Options.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Mask Names — Ask someone—or a shuffled Notice—to rename the leading options A, B and C without showing which is which.
2. Choose Traits — Choose three relevant traits, such as cost, time, fit, reliability, or learning. Keep safety facts visible.
3. Rank Blind — Compare the symbols on those traits without guessing their identities and Hold the current order.
4. Reveal Options — Reveal the names. Keep the blind order or name exactly what Name changed it and why.

FINISH MOVE — Reveal Options closes the round.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Do not over-score Hide The Option Names. The win is see what the options look like before their names start campaigning. End at Reveal Options.

1. Sort By Mind Mode — Group tasks into simple types such as talking, reading, errands, decisions, or admin.

3. Finish The Block — Complete that block before changing to a different kind of task.

items.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Precise — Choose an anchor and notice the precise moment contact breaks.
2. Return Instead — Instead of judging the distraction, shorten the delay before returning.
3. Track Interval — Track the interval between noticing and reconnection.
4. Let Practice — Let practice end after one stretch with visibly fewer or shorter gaps.

FINISH MOVE — Complete Let Practice, then return to your day.

items.title: BREAK THE NIGHT'S STORYLINE
items.name: BREAK THE NIGHT'S STORYLINE
items.hook: Break The Night'S Storyline loosens Narrative overbuilding. Purpose: Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.
items.recognition_cue: Break The Night'S Storyline loosens Narrative overbuilding. Purpose: Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.
items.goal: Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.
items.mission: Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.
items.challenge: Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.
items.immediate_need: Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.
items.game_move: Take Pick Word; keep Flash Image literal. After Jump Letter, return.
items.unique_game_move: Take Pick Word; keep Flash Image literal. After Jump Letter, return.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Rigid beliefs, labels & stories

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

HOOK
Break The Night'S Storyline loosens Narrative overbuilding. Purpose: Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.

GAME MOVE
Take Pick Word; keep Flash Image literal. After Jump Letter, return.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Pick Word — Choose one harmless five-letter word, such as TABLE. Use each letter once; there is no need to finish perfectly.
2. Call Object — For the first letter, name a neutral object beginning with it—T for tree, for example.
3. Flash Image — Picture that object for about two seconds with no action, meaning, memory, or story.
4. Jump Letter — Jump to the next letter and a completely unrelated object. End after five letters; do not score sleep.

FINISH MOVE — Jump Letter is your cue to stop.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Break The Night'S Storyline earns its finish: sleep does not need another storyline to solve. Once Jump Letter happens, stop.
items.formula_flow: Pick Word → Call Object → Flash Image → Jump Letter
items.safety:
PAUSE
Use only while safely resting; never while driving. Stop if images become distressing, compulsive, or disorienting.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

TRIGGER
Body-state misreading

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
The Action Had Many Authors loosens Body-state misreading. Work toward: Total doership omits most of the production team.

GOAL
Total doership omits most of the production team.

GAME MOVE
Take Name Conditions; keep Place Yourself literal. Do not pass Keep Responsibility.

1. Name Conditions — Review one action and name its conditions: intention, habit, body capacity, other people, tools, timing, culture, and chance.
2. Place Yourself — Place yourself among these causes rather than above them.
3. Keep Responsibility — Keep responsibility for your contribution while releasing sole authorship.

WIN SIGNAL
The Action Had Many Authors earns its finish: total doership omits most of the production team. Exit through Keep Responsibility.

FORMULA FLOW
Name Conditions → Place Yourself → Keep Responsibility

TRIGGER

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
Make The First Move Deliberately Wrong loosens Perfectionism. Keep the task narrow: A throwaway mistake can make the first move lose its authority.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A throwaway mistake can make the first move lose its authority.

GAME MOVE
Take Throwaway; keep Fix One literal. Stopping line: Continue Clean.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Throwaway — Open a private mental sandbox and mark it THROWAWAY—NOT FOR SENDING.
2. Make Wrong — Imagine one obviously imperfect start: a clumsy first sentence, rough title, messy mental sketch, or unfinished opening.
3. Fix One — Correct exactly one useful part without polishing the rest.
4. Continue Clean — Keep working only if the task now feels editable; otherwise keep the corrected fragment in mind and stop cleanly.

FINISH MOVE — Continue Clean is your cue to stop.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Make The First Move Deliberately Wrong earns its finish: a throwaway mistake can make the blank page lose its authority. Final marker: Continue Clean.
items.formula_flow: Throwaway → Make Wrong → Fix One → Continue Clean
items.safety:
PAUSE
Never use deliberate errors in medical, legal, financial, safety-critical, submitted, or live shared work.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

Identify Image frames it; Let Existing tests it. Close with Redirect.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Identify Image — Spot the image, conclusion, or demand being refreshed.
2. Time — For one minute, refuse only the renewal: no new scene, argument, or confirmation.
3. Let Existing — Let existing residue fade at its own rate.
4. Redirect — Redirect the freed attention into a chosen sensory task.

FINISH MOVE — Redirect is your cue to stop.

items.play_the_loop:
1. Underline — Underline absolutes and inflammatory terms in your account.
2. Observe Behaviour — Exchange every one for a precise factual equivalent: ‘always’ becomes the actual frequency; ‘destroyed’ becomes the specific loss; ‘evil’ becomes the observed behaviour.
3. Read Action — Re-read and notice what action the cooler version supports.

FINISH MOVE — Read Action is your cue to stop.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Absence becomes evidence only after prediction says what should be present.

GAME MOVE
Keep Ask Sign small; move through Mark Absence. Name Explanation lands; leave it.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Ask Sign — Ask what sign must exist right now if the feared model is correct.
2. Search Fairly — Search once, fairly.
3. Mark Absence — If it is absent, Keep that absence and reduce—not erase—the model’s weight.
4. Name Explanation — Name the alternate explanation strengthened by the missing sign.

FINISH MOVE — Name Explanation closes the round.

Look For The Missing Danger is useful when: absence becomes evidence only after prediction says what should be present. Let Name Explanation be enough.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Forecasts must compete for limited shelf space.

GAME MOVE
Keep Picture Predictions small; move through Cross Out. End when Act Portfolio completes.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Picture Predictions — Picture the three predictions currently most relevant.
2. Enter Retiring — Any new forecast may enter only by retiring one, merging with one, or proving higher usefulness for a decision.
3. Cross Out — Cross out retired entries visibly.
4. Act Portfolio — Act from the remaining portfolio rather than unlimited mental possibilities.

Let the space issue a clear instruction.

GAME MOVE
Identify Object to Remove Competing; no rewind. Close at Meet; do not restart.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Identify Object — Spot the first object the desired behaviour requires.
2. Position — Position it where normal movement will encounter it at the right time.
3. Remove Competing — Remove competing cues from that path.
4. Meet — When you meet the object, perform the linked first action before walking past.

GOAL
A safer choice may be the mistake you can see early enough to correct.

GAME MOVE
Name Options opens; Warning changes the angle. Last decision: Choose Visible.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Name Options — Name the two or three live options. For each, Picture the specific way it could fail—not a vague fear.
2. Name Failure — Name the earliest observable sign that failure has begun. It must be visible or clear, not a feeling alone.
3. Warning — State what corrective action would still be available when that sign appears and what cost has already accumulated.
4. Choose Visible — Prefer the option whose reliable warning arrives while correction is still practical. Use this as one decision criterion, not the whole verdict.

FINISH MOVE — Let Choose Visible be enough.

Let an unmoving object prove that movement is not the whole field.

GAME MOVE
Use Rest Gaze; stay concrete through Don't Match. Stop at Let Facts.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Rest Gaze — Rest your gaze on a stable line, corner, or heavy object.
2. Compare Visual — Compare its visual constancy with the motion inside your body and mind.
3. Don't Match — Do not make the inner movement match.
4. Let Facts — Let both facts coexist until the outer reference becomes usable.

FINISH MOVE — Let Let Facts be enough.

Use Identify Nearest; stay concrete through Move Attention. Endpoint: Let Far.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Identify Nearest — Spot the nearest sound, one mid-distance sound, and the farthest audible layer.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
See what the options look like before their names start campaigning.

GAME MOVE
Use Mask Names; stay concrete through Rank Blind. Last decision: Reveal Options.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Mask Names — Ask someone—or a shuffled Notice—to rename the leading options A, B and C without showing which is which.
2. Choose Traits — Choose three relevant traits, such as cost, time, fit, reliability, or learning. Keep safety facts visible.
3. Rank Blind — Compare the symbols on those traits without guessing their identities and Hold the current order.
4. Reveal Options — Reveal the names. Keep the blind order or name exactly what Name changed it and why.

FINISH MOVE — Reveal Options closes the round.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Do not over-score Hide The Option Names. The win is see what the options look like before their names start campaigning. End at Reveal Options.
items.formula_flow: Mask Names → Choose Traits → Rank Blind → Reveal Options
